turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's start with who decided Owen's essay gets a zero, and why I found out from my son instead of from you.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided, and when?
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
You're asking me to write your emails? Write it yourself, Hale; I'm here about Owen, and I still don't know what that zero is based on.
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
Flattery won't get you a ghostwriter, Hale. Either you tell me what that mark rests on, or I walk down to the principal's office right now and ask there.
